Daily Briefing — Friday, August 7 2026

Anthropic's $30B revenue milestone and enterprise AI governance crisis collide as EU AI Act enforcement begins.

AI & Technology

#1 — Anthropic expands Google Cloud partnership with multi-gigawatt compute commitment as revenue surges to $30B run-rate — Anthropic

★ Critical for Cristiano's AI product strategy: Anthropic's massive infrastructure investment reflects the capital demands of scaling agentic systems, directly relevant to enterprise AI adoption patterns at Eidosmedia.

Anthropic announced a major expansion with Google Cloud and Broadcom, planning multiple gigawatts of new compute capacity. The company's run-rate revenue has surpassed $30 billion (up from $9 billion end-2025), with enterprise customers spending over $1 million annually now exceeding 1,000 accounts—doubling in under two months.

#2 — Inference hooks now in beta for Claude Enterprise—AI governance layer for regulated organizations — Releasebot / Anthropic

★ Directly addresses Cristiano's governance mandate: inference hooks enable organizations to enforce security policies at the AI interaction layer—critical for regulated financial services and enterprise deployments.

Anthropic launched inference hooks in beta for Claude Enterprise, allowing organizations to route all governed prompts through their AI security server for approval before inference runs. Requests are signed, denials are recorded in compliance Activity Feeds, and failure handling is configurable.

Claude Ecosystem

#1 — Anthropic Economic Index connector launches for Claude—direct AI usage analytics in chat — Releasebot / Anthropic

★ Extends Claude's research and analytics capabilities: The Economic Index connector provides real-time labor market and AI adoption data—useful for personal OS productivity analysis and understanding which job functions are being automated.

Anthropic launched an Economic Index connector for Claude that lets users explore real-time AI adoption data directly in chat. The tool answers questions about occupations, tasks, and automation trends, with all answers grounded in the Index's source data.
